---
title: "Using pySEB"
subtitle: "Installation, visualization, portable models, and troubleshooting"
---

Use these pages when you need to set up pySEB, inspect a structure, save a
model, or resolve an error. For a worked modelling task, follow the
[Tutorials](tutorials/index.qmd).

## Installation

[Your first scattering model](tutorials/first-model.qmd#create-a-python-environment)
starts with Python environment setup on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including
the optional visualization dependencies and an import check.

For native C++ builds, optional symbolic backends, and platform-specific
dependencies, use the [platform build guides](https://github.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/wiki/Build-Guides).

## Visualization

[Visualization and OpenUSD](visualization.qmd) explains the interactive viewer,
model/unfolded layouts, reference markers, colors, opacity, and scene export.
The tutorial's first model introduces the controls beside its first 3D view.

## Save and reuse models

[Portable subunit definitions](file-defined-subunits.qmd) describes YAML model
files and validation. [Save, reload, and visualize a model](tutorials/save-load-model.qmd)
walks through preserving and restoring a complete structure.

## Troubleshooting

The [Troubleshooting and FAQ](https://github.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/wiki/Troubleshooting-and-FAQ)
covers import problems, unavailable backends, missing parameters, rejected
reference paths, and native build errors. For common first-run errors, see
[Common problems](tutorials/first-model.qmd#common-problems).

When reporting a problem, include the smallest model that reproduces it,
your Python and pySEB versions, the command you ran, and the complete error.
[Search or report an issue](https://github.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/issues).
